test_cases.name: Activate a customer-owned tablet with a physical SIM as a second line, end to end
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
BYOT (Bring Your Own Tablet) lets a store rep activate a tablet the customer already owns instead of selling dealer stock. It is the tablet branch of the BYOD path: an IMEI not found in dealer inventory is offered as customer-owned, the rep accepts and picks 'Tablet' from the BYOD device-type picker, and the platform registers the device with the carrier under the BYOT code at $0 device price (untaxed). Only the SIM, plan, taxes and accessories are charged. The rep's device-type selection is persisted through the whole activation and sent to the carrier (RTPL-2403 fix).

## Related tickets
RTPL-2205 (story), RTPL-2574, RTPL-2403 (PR #378), RTPL-2061 (BYOD Epic)

## Preconditions
- BYOD feature flag ON (ConfigCat enable_subscriber_activation_byod).
- Primary phone line activated on the order, then add-line performed — the tablet is line 2 (house rule: tablet/watch never line 1; note the backend has no hard gate, see Automation Notes).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Tablet IMEI:** First unused singleSims[] IMEI from simData<ENV>.json fixture pool (provisioned at Metro, not in dealer inventory, single-SIM device profile)
- **SIM (ICCID):** First unused iccids[] entry matching ^89[a-zA-Z0-9]{17}F$

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Teardown: afterEach cancels the line via apiCalls.cancelLine(processId); capture processId from the first lines/start intercept.
- Backend has NO hard primary-line gate for tablets — pairing logic is wearable-only and explicitly skipped for tablet lines (Engine.ConfigurePlan.cs:175-180; unit test Should_skip_pairing_when_byot_override_made_line_a_tablet). Primary-line-first is house convention / RTPOS parity, not a code guard — never author a line-1 tablet case, but do not expect a BE rejection either.
- Picker radio ids are stable automation hooks: #byod-device-type-BYOT etc. (select-byod-device-type.vue:151).
- BYOT pricing source: device-pricing-registry.ts:337-345 — sku 'BYOT-CUST', description 'Customer-Owned Tablet', basePrice 0, isTaxable false.
- Known blocker (2026-07-09 live run): tablet plan list returned plans:null at configure-plan (Bug #2). Re-verify on UAT3 before first automated run; the plan step must assert a non-empty list.
- Do NOT run against backend-mock: the mock still ships the RTPL-2403 device-type bug (collect-device-info-repository.ts:293-300) — real BE / UAT only.

test_cases.name: Phone-or-tablet BYOD picker offers exactly Android, iPhone and Tablet
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
When a rep accepts an unknown (non-watch) IMEI as customer-owned, the BYOD device-type picker must present the three selectable non-watch choices — BYOP Android, BYOP iPhone and Tablet. The backend also returns the disallowed BYOD-DSI code, which the frontend hides (product decision: no DSI). A missing Tablet option blocks every BYOT activation at the counter (RTPL-2574).

## Related tickets
RTPL-2574, RTPL-2205, RTPL-2403

## Preconditions
- BYOD feature flag ON (ConfigCat enable_subscriber_activation_byod).
- Primary phone line activated on the order, then add-line performed — the tablet candidate is line 2 (house rule).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Tablet IMEI:** First unused singleSims[] IMEI from simData<ENV>.json fixture pool (non-watch classification, not in dealer inventory)

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Partial case — stops at the picker assertion; no Order Summary / payment needed. Teardown: cancel the line via API.
- FE hides BYOD-DSI via HIDDEN_DEVICE_TYPES set (select-byod-device-type.vue:55) while the BE still returns it — assert the [BE] 4-code set AND the [FE] 3-radio render separately; both are regression signals.
- Labels come from ui.base.json byod-device-type.* keys — assert exact strings 'BYOP Android' / 'BYOP iPhone' / 'Tablet'.

steps.action: On the added line (line 2), rep enters the customer-owned tablet IMEI
steps.expected: [Both] POST validate-device -> device not in dealer inventory; actions [accept-add-as-byod, decline-add-as-byod] offered. [FE] Drawer title 'IMEI not found'

steps.action: Rep continues, accepting the device as customer-owned (BYOD)
steps.expected: [BE] POST collect-device-info {action:'accept-add-as-byod'} -> reasonCodeForAction='select-byod-device-type'; availableByodDeviceTypes=['BYOD-ANDROID','BYOD-IPHONE','BYOD-DSI','BYOT'] (exact set, order-insensitive)

steps.action: Rep inspects the device type picker screen
steps.expected: [FE] Title 'Add BYOD device'; label 'Select device type'; description 'Select the device type to register this device as a BYOD (Bring Your Own Device).'; EXACTLY 3 radio options rendered: 'BYOP Android' (#byod-device-type-BYOD-ANDROID), 'BYOP iPhone' (#byod-device-type-BYOD-IPHONE), 'Tablet' (#byod-device-type-BYOT); NO 'BYOD-DSI' option visible; all 3 selectable; Continue label = 'Continue'

test_cases.name: Tablet option appears in the watch-compatible BYOD picker
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
Legacy RTPOS offers Tablet in the watch-compatible BYOD picker, and RTGO must match: when the carrier classifies the customer-owned IMEI as a watch, the device-type picker shows the watch options AND Tablet — because watch-classified tablets exist in the wild and the rep must be able to correct the classification. Before the RTPL-2574 fix only the two smartwatch choices appeared, dead-ending tablet activations that arrived through this branch.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2574 (fix), RTPL-2205, RTPL-2557

## Preconditions
- BYOD feature flag ON (ConfigCat enable_subscriber_activation_byod).
- Primary phone line activated on the order, then add-line performed — the device is line 2 (house rule).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Watch IMEI:** Real watch IMEI from the RTGO Data workbook that Metro resolves with watch classification (byodType 'W'); probe live — do not synthesize

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Partial case — stops at the picker assertion. Teardown: cancel the line via API.
- MUST run against the real backend: backend-mock's watch branch returns only ['BYOW-SAM','BYOW-APPLEWATCH'] — the RTPL-2574 fix is NOT in the mock (collect-device-info-repository.ts:169-173), and mock tests lock in the wrong behavior. A mock run fails this case falsely.
- Real-BE source of truth: GetAvailableWatchOptions includes BYOT in both DSI and non-DSI variants (SubscriberActivationConstants.cs:126-132, comment cites RTPL-2574).

steps.action: On the added line (line 2), rep enters the watch-classified customer-owned IMEI
steps.expected: [Both] POST validate-device -> device not in dealer inventory, watch classification (isWatch=true); actions [accept-add-as-byod, decline-add-as-byod] offered. [FE] Drawer title 'IMEI not found'

steps.action: Rep continues, accepting the device as customer-owned (BYOD)
steps.expected: [BE] reasonCodeForAction='select-byod-device-type'; availableByodDeviceTypes = ['BYOW-SAM','BYOW-APPLEWATCH','BYOT'] (non-DSI watch set — Tablet MUST be present)

steps.action: Rep inspects the device type picker screen
steps.expected: [FE] Exactly 3 radios rendered: 'BYOW Sam', 'BYOW Apple Watch', 'Tablet' (#byod-device-type-BYOT); all selectable

test_cases.name: Choosing Tablet for a watch-classified device reclassifies the line and skips watch pairing
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
When the carrier classifies a customer-owned device as a watch but the rep picks Tablet from the picker, the platform must override the classification: the line becomes a Tablet (selectedByodDeviceType 'BYOT', deviceType 'Tablet'), watch plan filtering and wearable pairing no longer apply, and the carrier receives the tablet code as-is (no Samsung watch item-id substitution). This is the correction path for tablets that Metro's device database mis-tags as wearables.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2574, RTPL-2403, RTPL-2347 (pairing), RTPL-2576 (watch eSIM)

## Preconditions
- BYOD feature flag ON (ConfigCat enable_subscriber_activation_byod).
- Primary phone line activated on the order, then add-line performed — the device is line 2 (house rule).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Watch IMEI:** Real watch IMEI from the RTGO Data workbook that Metro resolves with watch classification (byodType 'W')

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Known asymmetry (potential product bug — raise before automating the SIM assertion hard): the BYOT override flips DeviceType to Tablet but leaves IsWatch=true, and BuildAllowedSimOptions passes IsWatch (Engine.ValidateDevice.cs:898-913) — so this line still gets the watch eSIM-only SIM matrix. Backend unit test Should_skip_pairing_when_byot_override_made_line_a_tablet (WhenValidatingPairingSelection.cs:130-144) proves the pairing skip; nothing pins the SIM matrix. Confirm intended behavior with product, then harden step 4.
- Override source: Engine.CollectDeviceInfo.cs:302-312 (IsWatch branch: BYOT -> DeviceType.Tablet); no-substitution rule: DeviceState.cs:186-205 ('BYOT is sent to AddByodDevice as-is').
- Real BE only — mock lacks the 2574/2403 behavior.
- Partial case — stops at the plan-list assertion; no payment.

steps.action: On the added line (line 2), rep enters the watch-classified IMEI, accepts as BYOD, and reaches the picker
steps.expected: [BE] availableByodDeviceTypes includes 'BYOT'. [FE] Picker shows 'BYOW Sam', 'BYOW Apple Watch', 'Tablet'

steps.action: Rep selects 'Tablet' (selection only)
steps.expected: [FE] #byod-device-type-BYOT checked; Continue enabled; no advance

steps.action: Rep taps Continue
steps.expected: [Both] POST collect-device-info {action:'select-byod-device-type', inputData:{deviceType:'BYOT'}} -> deviceValidationDetails: selectedByodDeviceType='BYOT', deviceType='Tablet' (overridden from Wearable), isByod=true. Carrier device-create receives 'BYOT' as-is — NO Samsung QuantomItemId substitution. [FE] Flow advances toward SIM validation

steps.action: Rep observes the SIM validation step presented for the reclassified line
steps.expected: [FE] SIM validation renders. RECORD which SIM matrix appears: code keys SIM options on isWatch, which REMAINS true after the tablet override — so the watch (eSIM/EID) matrix is expected today. Flag the observed behavior; do not fail the case on it (open product question)

steps.action: Rep proceeds to Plan selection (via SIM + MDN per the observed matrix)
steps.expected: [BE] Wearable pairing does NOT run — no pairing-mdn-* reason codes, no 'availableSubscriberForPairing' requirement; plan list is the tablet/standard list, not watch plans (no AWATCH*/FAMWATCH SOC codes)

test_cases.name: Dual-IMEI tablet prompts for the second IMEI before the device is created
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
The second-IMEI prompt in the BYOD tablet path is conditional: it appears only when the device profile marks a dual-IMEI device (carrier deviceProperty starting 'DF' or 'DS'). For those devices the rep must supply IMEI2 after picking Tablet, and the platform pre-fills it when the carrier already knows it. Devices without the dual-IMEI property skip the prompt entirely (covered by the companion case).

## Related tickets
RTPL-2205 (AC-5/AC-6 IMEI2 conditioning), RTPL-2403

## Preconditions
- BYOD feature flag ON (ConfigCat enable_subscriber_activation_byod).
- Primary phone line activated on the order, then add-line performed — the tablet is line 2 (house rule).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Tablet IMEI (IMEI1):** dualSims[].imei1 from simData<ENV>.json fixture pool (dual-IMEI device profile, deviceProperty DF/DS)
- **IMEI2:** dualSims[].imei2 from the same fixture-pool entry

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Prompt gate: IsDualImeiDeviceProperty = deviceProperty startsWith DF|DS (Engine.CollectDeviceInfo.cs:320-352); FE renders on reasonCodeForAction only (collect-device-info.vue:41-42).
- Known parity gap (doc RTPL-2403 plan :58): legacy sends [imei1, imei2] to the carrier device-create; RTGO sends [imei2] only. If carrier-side assertions are added later, expect the single-element list.
- Teardown: cancel the line via API.

steps.action: On the added line (line 2), rep enters IMEI1, accepts as BYOD, selects 'Tablet' and taps Continue
steps.expected: [Both] select-byod-device-type accepted (selectedByodDeviceType='BYOT'); because deviceProperty starts DF/DS the flow does NOT create the device yet — reasonCodeForAction='provide-imei2-for-byod' with action [provide-imei2]. [FE] IMEI2 screen: title 'Add BYOD device', description starts 'The device entered was not found by the compatibility checker, or the checker is currently unavailable.'; IMEI2 field pre-filled when the carrier returned one

steps.action: Rep confirms/enters the second IMEI and continues
steps.expected: [Both] POST collect-device-info {action:'provide-imei2'} -> device created (isByod=true, deviceSource='B'); collect-device-info completes and the flow advances through resolve-device-pricing to 'SIM validation'

test_cases.name: Single-SIM tablet skips the second-IMEI prompt
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
Complement of the dual-IMEI case: when the device profile carries no dual-IMEI marker (deviceProperty not starting 'DF'/'DS'), picking Tablet creates the customer-owned device immediately — the rep is never asked for a second IMEI. Prompting for data the device does not have slows the counter and confuses reps, so the absence of the prompt is itself the assertion.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2205 (AC-7 IMEI2 skipped), RTPL-2403

## Preconditions
- BYOD feature flag ON (ConfigCat enable_subscriber_activation_byod).
- Primary phone line activated on the order, then add-line performed — the tablet is line 2 (house rule).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Tablet IMEI:** First unused singleSims[] IMEI from simData<ENV>.json fixture pool (single-SIM device profile)

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Assert the NEGATIVE: intercept collect-device-info responses and require reasonCodeForAction never equals 'provide-imei2-for-byod' before SIM validation.
- Gate source: Engine.CollectDeviceInfo.cs:320-333 (non-dual property -> EnsureByodEnabled -> CreateByodDeviceAndComplete).
- Teardown: cancel the line via API.

steps.action: On the added line (line 2), rep enters the IMEI, accepts as BYOD, selects 'Tablet' and taps Continue
steps.expected: [Both] select-byod-device-type -> device created in the SAME activity completion (no intermediate action): NO provide-imei2-for-byod reason code ever appears in the response stream; deviceValidationDetails: selectedByodDeviceType='BYOT', isByod=true. [FE] No IMEI2 screen renders; flow lands directly on 'SIM validation'

test_cases.name: Second-IMEI entry rejects empty and wrong-length values
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
The IMEI2 field on the BYOD tablet path validates server-side: the value is required and must be exactly 15 digits. Boundary values around the 15-digit rule (14, 16, empty, non-numeric) must be rejected with the exact validator messages, and the rep must be able to correct the value and proceed without restarting the line.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2205, RTPL-2403

## Preconditions
- BYOD feature flag ON (ConfigCat enable_subscriber_activation_byod).
- Primary phone line activated on the order, then add-line performed — the tablet is line 2 (house rule).
- Rep has reached the IMEI2 prompt (dual-IMEI tablet, 'Tablet' selected).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Tablet IMEI (IMEI1):** dualSims[].imei1 from simData<ENV>.json fixture pool
- **Valid IMEI2:** dualSims[].imei2 from the same entry
- **Invalid IMEI2 values:** Empty string; 14 digits (valid IMEI2 minus last digit); 16 digits (valid IMEI2 plus one digit); 15 chars with a letter

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Validator source: SubscriberActivationEngine.CollectDeviceInfo.cs:27-39 (NotEmpty + ^\d{15}$ with the two exact messages).
- RTGO error toasts auto-dismiss — assert on the intercepted 4xx response body, not by polling the DOM later.
- Partial case — stops after recovery; no payment. Teardown: cancel the line via API.

steps.action: Rep clears the IMEI2 field and submits empty
steps.expected: [Both] provide-imei2 rejected 400 with validator message 'IMEI2 is required.'; line state unchanged (reasonCodeForAction still 'provide-imei2-for-byod'). [FE] Error surfaces as an auto-dismissing top-right toast — capture synchronously on the 4xx

steps.action: Rep submits a 14-digit value
steps.expected: [Both] Rejected 400 with 'IMEI2 must be exactly 15 digits.'; state unchanged

steps.action: Rep submits a 16-digit value
steps.expected: [Both] Rejected 400 with 'IMEI2 must be exactly 15 digits.'; state unchanged

steps.action: Rep submits 15 characters containing a letter
steps.expected: [Both] Rejected 400 with 'IMEI2 must be exactly 15 digits.' (regex ^\d{15}$); state unchanged

steps.action: Rep enters the valid IMEI2 and continues
steps.expected: [Both] provide-imei2 accepted; device created; flow advances to 'SIM validation' — recovery works without restarting the line

test_cases.name: A device type that was not offered to the line is rejected and the rep can recover
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
The backend validates the rep's device-type choice twice: the code must be one of the seven known BYOD codes, and it must be in the set offered to THIS line (a watch code cannot be forced onto a phone/tablet line and vice versa). An invalid submission returns a 400 without mutating the line, so the rep's next valid pick — Tablet — still succeeds. The UI never renders un-offered options, so this guard is exercised at the API level.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2205, RTPL-2556 (guard), RTPL-2403

## Preconditions
- BYOD feature flag ON (ConfigCat enable_subscriber_activation_byod).
- Primary phone line activated on the order, then add-line performed — the tablet is line 2 (house rule).
- Rep has reached the device-type picker on a non-watch line (offered set = BYOD-ANDROID, BYOD-IPHONE, BYOD-DSI, BYOT).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Tablet IMEI:** First unused singleSims[] IMEI from simData<ENV>.json fixture pool (non-watch classification)

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Guard sources: NormalizeDeviceType null -> throw (Engine.CollectDeviceInfo.cs:277-282); not-in-offered-set -> throw (:284-293). Both raise InvalidByodDeviceTypeException (400).
- Mock parity: mock returns 400 code 'invalid-activity-action' with message listing the 7 valid values (collect-device-info-service.ts:132-141) — message text differs from real BE; assert status + state, not message, if mock is ever used.
- State-integrity recovery mirrors RTPL-2556 TC-5. Teardown: cancel the line via API.

steps.action: Via API, submit a watch code not offered to this line
steps.expected: [BE] 400 invalid BYOD device type (InvalidByodDeviceTypeException — code not in the offered set); deviceValidationDetails unchanged: selectedByodDeviceType null, deviceType NOT reclassified

steps.action: Via API, submit an unknown code
steps.expected: [BE] 400 invalid BYOD device type (normalization returns null for unknown codes); state unchanged; reasonCodeForAction still 'select-byod-device-type'

steps.action: Rep selects 'Tablet' in the UI and taps Continue
steps.expected: [Both] select-byod-device-type {deviceType:'BYOT'} accepted; selectedByodDeviceType='BYOT'; no residual state from the rejected attempts; flow advances normally

test_cases.name: Declining the customer-owned offer aborts the tablet line cleanly
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
When the platform offers to register an unknown IMEI as customer-owned and the rep declines (customer changed their mind, wrong IMEI typed), the line must abort cleanly: the decline action returns a validation-aborted failure, no BYOD device is created, and the rep can restart with a different IMEI. A dirty abort would strand half-created lines on the account.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2205, RTPL-2061

## Preconditions
- BYOD feature flag ON (ConfigCat enable_subscriber_activation_byod).
- Primary phone line activated on the order, then add-line performed — the tablet candidate is line 2 (house rule).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Tablet IMEI:** First unused singleSims[] IMEI from simData<ENV>.json fixture pool (not in dealer inventory)

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Decline source: Engine.CollectDeviceInfo.cs:262-265 (decline-add-as-byod -> ValidationAbortedException, HTTP 400).
- The decline path is also reachable via decline-add-to-edge -> edge-declined-offer-byod -> same accept/decline pair (Engine :209-233) — one case covers the guard; note the second entry point for exploratory runs.
- Teardown: cancel the line via API if any line state persists.

steps.action: On the added line (line 2), rep enters the IMEI and reaches the customer-owned offer
steps.expected: [Both] validate-device -> actions [accept-add-as-byod, decline-add-as-byod]. [FE] 'IMEI not found' drawer visible

steps.action: Rep declines the customer-owned offer (goes back)
steps.expected: [Both] POST collect-device-info {action:'decline-add-as-byod'} -> 400 validation-aborted (ValidationAbortedException); NO device created (deviceValidationDetails has no selectedByodDeviceType, no isByod=true device row in the cart). [FE] Error toast on the 4xx; rep is returned to IMEI entry — capture the toast synchronously

steps.action: Rep enters a different valid IMEI on the same line
steps.expected: [Both] validate-device runs fresh — no residual BYOD state from the declined attempt; the flow proceeds normally

test_cases.name: With the BYOD feature off, a customer-owned tablet cannot enter the flow
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
The whole customer-owned path is gated by the BYOD feature flag. With the flag off, an IMEI not found in dealer inventory must NOT be offered as customer-owned — the device is unsupported and the rep is directed to RTPOS. This protects stores from starting activations the backend will refuse to complete. There is no separate backend tablet flag: tablets ride the single BYOD gate.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2205 (AC-1 gate), RTPL-2061

## Preconditions
- ConfigCat enable_subscriber_activation_byod OFF for the test store/environment.
- Primary phone line activated on the order, then add-line performed — the tablet candidate is line 2 (house rule).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **Tablet IMEI:** First unused singleSims[] IMEI from simData<ENV>.json fixture pool (not in dealer inventory)

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Feature description
A customer-owned tablet carries no device charge: the platform prices it as 'Customer-Owned Tablet' at $0.00 with no device tax. The physical SIM is NOT free on the BYOD path — it sells at $10 with no auto-discount and is taxed on the $10 selling price (unlike A-Stock where the SIM is discounted to free). The cart and device drilldown must show these numbers exactly; wrong SIM pricing on BYOD lines is a recurring regression.

test_cases.name: A dealer-stock tablet bypasses the customer-owned flow entirely
test_cases.custom_requirements:
## Feature description
Contrast/regression guard for the BYOT feature: a tablet that IS in dealer inventory (A-Stock) must never be routed into the customer-owned path. Entering a catalog tablet IMEI goes straight to SIM validation — no 'IMEI not found' drawer, no accept-as-BYOD offer, no device-type picker — and the device keeps its catalog price. A catalog tablet appearing in the BYOD flow means inventory resolution broke.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2141 (A-Stock tablet), RTPL-2205, RTPL-2061

## Preconditions
- BYOD feature flag ON (ConfigCat enable_subscriber_activation_byod) — the bypass must hold even with BYOD enabled.
- Primary phone line activated on the order, then add-line performed — the tablet is line 2 (house rule).

## Test Data (FE — what the rep types)
- **A-Stock tablet IMEI:** Unused catalog tablet IMEI from the RTGO Data workbook (probe live — 'Used' column lies)
- **SIM (ICCID):** First unused iccids[] entry

_All other values (device type, MDN, plan, coupon, protection, add-on) are discovered at run time — not pinned._

## Automation Notes
- Assert the ABSENCE of the BYOD drawer/picker — a tablet routed into collect-device-info here is the regression signal.
- Routing source: NextActivityMap — validate-device goes to collect-device-info only on NeedsEdgeCreation|NeedsByodCreation|NeedsEid, else resolve-device-pricing (SubscriberActivationProcessConfiguration.cs:55-61).
- Adjacent edge (not this case): a previously-activated A-Stock tablet in local inventory auto-accepts reactivation without a prompt (Engine.ValidateDevice.cs:586-599) — candidate for the Tablet/A-Stock suite, out of BYOT scope.
- Teardown: cancel the line via API.
